pull.title: validation: return block-file flush errors
pull.body:
**Problem:** When flushing block or undo data fails, `FlushStateToDisk()` still writes block-index metadata and coins data, then advances `m_last_flushed_block`.
With a separate `-blocksdir`, persistent failures there can leave metadata referring to block data that is not durable even when chainstate writes succeed.

**Fix:** Return the flush error before those writes, leaving the last-flushed marker and on-disk coins tip unchanged in the failing call.
Later flushes can retry and write if they succeed, including during shutdown.
`ConnectTip()` and `DisconnectTip()` propagate the error before updating the chain tip, after applying the coins changes in memory.

**History:**
* [#27866](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/27866#discussion_r1297313148) raised whether saving other state after a flush failure was preferable. This change preserves later retries while skipping writes in the failing call.
* [#34897](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34897) introduced `m_last_flushed_block` to prevent persistent indexes from advancing past flushed chainstate. This fix keeps it at the last successful flush.

Concept ACK

I still have to dig into the code and the implications of this change (just did a quick review), but in the meantime: would it be worth adding a test case for the undo-file failure path as well?  both the commit message and the error string mention block or undo files, but the test only injects a failure on blk*.dat.

I opened a follow-up PR https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35731 i did while reviewing the PR with the intention to group this notify + `state.Error()` behaviour into one helper, (making the invariant of the comment harder) and add more low-level tests like the ones you mentioned above.

It would be good to discuss the real-world consequences of this change a bit more:

As far as I understand one reason for the status quo is that even if an error would occur, and the data is not durable, there is a good chance of the fsync being done by the OS eventually if the failure is temporary - data is not necessarily lost, so we might as well flush the other state to avoid having to re-do the syncing. If the failure was permanent, the other write operations (chainstate etc.) would likely fail as well, so nothing gets out of sync in that scenario either.

However, one point for this change is that block data is often stored separately (`-blocksdir` option). In this case, it is quite possible that actually corruption occurs if the `blocksdir` fsync fails permanently, but flushes of the chainstate etc. all succeed, and `BLOCK_HAVE_DATA` is set in the blocktree db, while the actual block data is missing.

So I am Concept ACK

Concept ACK (e1a337ee961db4308697de7cddcf4aad9684c7f1)

The change is within `FlushStateToDisk`, and changes how an error from `FlushChainstateBlockFile` is handled -- ignored previously, returned upwards with the change.

Build & unit tests verfied locally.

The effectiveness of the new test (i.e., it catches the error) is checked by manually reverting the change.

Analyis of call pattern of `FlushChainstateBlockFile`: directly called in only one place, the one affected in this change.
Indirectly it is used in several usecases:

- The chain tip advances (connect/disconnect, including during IBD/reorgs),
- A new block is accepted to disk,
- The mempool cache is trimmed after accepting transactions/packages,
- A user manually prunes via RPC,
- The coins cache is resized,
- An assumeutxo snapshot finishes background validation,
- The node shuts down or an RPC/kernel-API caller explicitly forces a flush.

It's hard to conceptually assess the high-level effects in all the use cases.

Reviewing the steps excluded with the early exit, the update of the `m_next_write` seems uneqivocal, it _may_ have unintended consequences (left comment).

LGTM, left some comments.
Thanks for the review, took me a bit longer to react, I'm juggling a few open ones...

ACK c42d7fe1cf2aee821b4f9931ef94f16e09de8459

Concluding my previous review. Reviewed, built and unit-tested locally. Also verified that without the behavior change, the new test fails.

Code review ACK 12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056. Thanks for putting the test first, it makes the behavior change easy to verify.

This reverses my suggestion from https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/27866#discussion_r1297313148 when that PR was trying to make the same change. But that suggestion was mainly based on not wanting to have an unjustified behavior change in a cleanup PR, and now there is a clear justification.

Left some comments below, but none blocking. I think this should be merged given all the review it's had so far.

Post-merge, here is a list of possible follow-ups, roughly in order of importance. It collects suggestions from the review comments above, mine and other reviewers', and from follow-up PRs. Items 1-3 can crash the node or leave a corrupt database on disk; I reproduced each with a unit test. The rest are smaller bugs, documentation and tests. Happy to review any of these.

1. **`ConnectTip()` and `DisconnectTip()` should not return early on a flush failure after updating `CoinsTip()`.** Both apply the block to `CoinsTip()`, then return false on a flush error before `m_chain.SetTip()` ([disconnect](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L2975-L2978), [connect](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L3068-L3071)), so a disk error leaves the coins tip and the chain tip pointing at different blocks until shutdown.

   I checked this with a unit test: after a block file flush failure inside `ConnectTip()`, submitting a transaction aborts on the [`PreChecks()` assert](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L876), and creating a block template aborts on the [`ConnectBlock()` assert](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L2330-L2332) through `TestBlockValidity()`. So a transaction or `getblocktemplate` call arriving before shutdown finishes can crash the node instead of letting it shut down cleanly.

   Returning false here treats a disk failure as if it were a memory failure. Memory and disk each need to be consistent on their own, and disk normally lags behind memory; a failed flush only means it lags further. These functions should ignore the flush result the way `AcceptBlock()` does (the error is already reported through `flushError()`), and let `ActivateBestChain()` stop on the interrupt as usual. This predates the PR: the `CheckDiskSpace()` failure already returned from the same place. ([original suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r4405681713))

2. **A failed coins DB write can drop changes from memory, which can then leave a corrupt UTXO set on disk or crash the node.** [`CCoinsViewCache::Sync()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/coins.cpp#L284-L293), used for periodic and prune flushes, writes the cache to the database in several batches through [`CCoinsViewDB::BatchWrite()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/txdb.cpp#L135-L198). As each entry is added to a batch, the cache stops tracking it as needing a write (spent coins are erased, other entries marked clean), before the batch is committed.

   If a commit [throws](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/dbwrapper.cpp#L319-L320) on a LevelDB write error, the changes in that batch are neither in the cache nor on disk, so the cache serves those spent coins from the database as unspent. `FlushStateToDisk()` [catches the error](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L2841-L2843) and requests shutdown, but the node keeps running until then. If a later flush at the same block succeeds, like the shutdown flush, it writes the remaining entries and records the database as consistent at that block without the lost batch. If a block is connected first, the flush aborts on an [assert](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/txdb.cpp#L150) instead.

   I checked this with a unit test against a real on-disk `CCoinsViewDB`, making one write fail partway through the flush. After the failed `Sync()`, 29 of 200 coins spent in the new block were visible as unspent through the cache. The successful retry then recorded the database as consistent at the new block, with those 29 spent coins still in it. A restart would load that as a valid UTXO set.

   This predates the PR and is a different code path, but it breaks the same rule as item 1: a disk failure shouldn't change memory. Keeping entries dirty until their batch commits would fix it.

3. **A failed block index write drops pending block index updates, which can leave a node that won't start without a reindex.** As in item 2, [`WriteBlockIndexDB()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/node/blockstorage.cpp#L529-L546) erases `m_dirty_fileinfo` and `m_dirty_blockindex` before `WriteBatchSync()` writes them. If that write throws, the block index and file info updates are no longer marked dirty, so a later flush skips them. The shutdown flush retry can succeed, and it then writes the coins on top of a block index on disk that is missing the updates.

   I checked this with a unit test: after a failed block index write and a successful retry, the coins DB's best block was the new tip but the new tip wasn't in the block index on disk. After a simulated restart, the node failed to start with "Error initializing block database" and needed a reindex.

   Clearing the dirty sets only after the write succeeds would fix it.

4. **Document how callers should use the `FlushStateToDisk()` return value.** The [header comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.h#L736-L750) only says "@returns true unless a system error occurred", which doesn't tell callers what a false return means for the state they hold. Items 1 and 8 are callers that misread it. Maybe something like:
   ```
   * @returns false if state could not be written to disk. The error has
   *     already been reported through the kernel notifications (in the node
   *     this requests shutdown).
   *
   * @warning The return value only says whether state was written to disk;
   *     in-memory state is valid either way. A caller whose own return value
   *     says whether it updated in-memory state should not return false just
   *     because this did.
   ```

5. **Tests that inject a failure at each write and check memory and disk afterwards.** These would have caught items 1-3. Fail each write point in turn (block file, undo file, block index batch, each coins batch, including partial batches), then check that memory is still consistent (`CoinsTip()` best block matches `m_chain.Tip()`, the coins view matches the expected UTXO set) and that a restart, or a retry where that's allowed, ends up with the same state on disk as a run with no failure. A test-only option to fail the Nth database write, next to the existing `simulate_crash_ratio`, would make the database cases easy.

   This also covers checking that a flush after a failed one succeeds and writes the skipped state, which isn't tested yet ([original suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r4403889247)). @arejula27 mentioned writing a test like this locally, so it might fit in [#35731](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35731).

6. **Comments that say why the flush handling is right.** The [`AcceptBlock()` comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L4399-L4405) still refers to "the fatal error notification", and describes ignoring the result as keeping callers from mistreating a flush failure. Ignoring the result is more than defensive: callers rely on the return value to know whether the block was stored and the block index updated. If a flush error could make it return false after those updates, the return value would stop meaning anything, which would be bad for composability even though no current caller would break. Maybe something like this ([original suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r4405809581)):
   ```
   // Ignore flush errors. By this point the block is stored and the block
   // index updated, and callers rely on the return value to know that.
   // Failing to write state to disk doesn't undo that, and FlushStateToDisk()
   // has already reported the error through flushError() or fatalError().
   ```
   Separately, the new early return in `FlushStateToDisk()` could say why returning is recoverable: the skipped writes stay in memory and a later flush, like the one at shutdown, can write them ([original suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r4405409912)).

7. **Pruned block files aren't deleted if a prune flush fails and a later flush succeeds.** `FindFilesToPrune()` updates the in-memory file info before the flush, but `setFilesToPrune` is a local, so the retry writes the index and never [unlinks the files](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L2795-L2799). The disk-space failure already had this gap; this PR adds the block-file failure as a second trigger. Keeping the pending set as a member that `UnlinkPrunedFiles()` drains after the next successful `WriteBlockIndexDB()` would fix it ([original suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r4403913190)).

   I checked this with a unit test using `-prune=1 -fastprune`: after a manual prune whose flush failed and a successful retry, `blk00000.dat` was still there, while the same prune with no failure deletes it.

8. **`ActivateBestChain()` returns false after its own periodic flush fails, even though the blocks it connected are fully applied in memory.** The [periodic flush](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L3463-L3465) returns false on failure, while stopping on the [interrupt](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L3489-L3494) returns true, so callers report a failure for blocks that were connected: the `generate*` RPCs say "block not accepted", and the kernel API's `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block()` returns an error.

   This matches the documentation ("@returns true unless a system error occurred"), but it makes false ambiguous: callers can't tell a failed disk write from a block that couldn't be connected. The disk failure is already reported through `flushError()`, so returning it again doesn't tell callers anything new. It should ignore the flush result like `AcceptBlock()` and let the interrupt check end the loop, so that false only means a block couldn't be connected or disconnected. The documentation could then say that disk write failures are reported through the notifications instead.

9. **Document that kernel API users should stop validation after a flush or fatal error.** Some validation code is [only](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L3215-L3219) [safe](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L3254-L3258) because the node's [`flushError()` and `fatalError()` handlers](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/node/kernel_notifications.cpp#L92-L101) request shutdown, which sets the interrupt that validation checks. Kernel API users provide their own handlers, which may not request shutdown ([earlier comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r4403889605)). The [`btck_NotifyFlushError`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h#L558-L559) and fatal error callbacks could document that the embedder should call `btck_context_interrupt()` and stop submitting blocks and transactions after one fires, as the node does. That is simpler than making validation correct without it, which would add code the node doesn't need.

10. **`MaybeValidateSnapshot()` should check its flush result before hashing the coins DB.** It calls [`ForceFlushStateToDisk()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L6038), which only logs a failure, then hashes `CoinsDB()` ([original suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r4403889053)). After a failed flush the DB is behind the tip, so the hash doesn't match and the snapshot chainstate is discarded as invalid. In the node this doesn't happen, because the shutdown request [stops the hashing](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/validation.cpp#L6053-L6061) first, but that depends on the interrupt being set, not on anything this function checks.

    It should return early with a new `SnapshotCompletionResult` when the flush fails, without discarding anything. `LoadChainstate()` [calls `MaybeValidateSnapshot()` again](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/node/chainstate.cpp#L204-L206) at the next startup, so the check is retried.

11. **[#35731](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35731) (@arejula27): `BlockManager`-level tests and a notify-and-error helper.** This covers the undo-file failure path @arejula27 asked about in [this comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#issuecomment-4962258493), which @l0rinc deferred to a lower-level test. It needs a rebase now that this is merged.

12. **RPCs that label a possibly stale coins DB with the in-memory tip.** `scantxoutset` ([code](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L2476-L2478)) and `CreateRolledBackUTXOSnapshot()` ([code](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9bf4815b94b9eaf8807f4e569091778da6c338d5/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L3286)) ignore the `ForceFlushStateToDisk()` result, then read `CoinsDB()` and report it as `m_chain.Tip()`. After a failed flush the DB is at the previous flush. Minor, since the node is shutting down. If this isn't changed, the RPC help could warn that the result may lag the tip.

13. **Test style (@maflcko, @optout21).** @maflcko [suggested](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r3802387955) splitting the `&&` in the test's `BOOST_CHECK` to follow the style from [#35729](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35729) and avoid a silent conflict with the Boost removal in [#35713](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35713). @optout21 [suggested](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#discussion_r3810102050) a `BOOST_CHECK_ALL`-style macro that prints every value when one condition fails. Neither change was made; this only matters when [#35713](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35713) is rebased.

comments.body:
> would it be worth adding a test case for the undo-file failure path as well

Good question, thanks - `FlushBlockFile()` returns false for either block or undo flush failures, see: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/e1a337ee961db4308697de7cddcf4aad9684c7f1/src/node/blockstorage.cpp#L774-L786
Since this PR only changes how that shared result is handled, testing both failure sources separately would fit better in a lower-level `BlockManager` test.
nit in 0f04fbee2f123c37c4b6fbff7dc10f61dd0b5924: The `&&` make this a bit harder to read and violate https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35729

`flushed` is tied to the `state` being invalid, it makes more sense to test them in groups, see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35729#pullrequestreview-4715961548

If you insist I can remove the `state` validation here.

> [0f04fbe](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714/changes/0f04fbee2f123c37c4b6fbff7dc10f61dd0b5924) _test: characterize writes after flush failure_:

Unit test observation: Running all 781 unit tests, they all pass, but a single output line is printed on the output:
`Error: A fatal internal error occurred, see debug.log for details: Flushing block file to disk failed. This is likely the result of an I/O error.`
This is noted as this is the only stdout printout from the whole unit test suite. It is emitted from the new unit test (`chainstate_flush_failure_boundary` -> 2ns call to `FlushStateToDisk` -> `FlushChainstateBlockFile` -> `FlushBlockFile`.)
Any chance to suppress this?

> [0f04fbe](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714/changes/0f04fbee2f123c37c4b6fbff7dc10f61dd0b5924) _test: characterize writes after flush failure_:

Why not simply `BOOST_CHECK(flushed); BOOST_CHECK(state.IsValid());` ?

> [e1a337e](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714/changes/e1a337ee961db4308697de7cddcf4aad9684c7f1) _validation: stop writes after flush failure_:

Why is the `LogWarning` removed? I could not convince myself that the `fatalError()`/`state.Error()` calls include the same logging. Is it possible to preserve the log line?

At first I though that the added comments refers to the reason of removal of `LogWarning`, but then I realized it explains the usage of `state.Error()` instead of `FatalError()`.

Regarding the comment, `FlushChainstateBlockFile` indeed calls `KernelNotifications::flushError` whenever it returns `false`, but this is handled across two levels (`FlushUndoFile`), which is a bit too brittle.

> [e1a337e](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714/changes/e1a337ee961db4308697de7cddcf4aad9684c7f1) _validation: stop writes after flush failure_:

With this early exit, the update of `m_next_write` below is also skipped. It looks like that _may_ cause some unwanted side-effects, so maybe it should be kept (e.g. by storing the return value, skipping the steps to be skipped, and keeping the `if (should_write || m_next_write == ...` block).

- [`ActivateBestChain()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056/src/validation.cpp#L3463-L3466) returns false. - [`AcceptBlock()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056/src/validation.cpp#L4399-L4405) ignores the result, with a comment saying the notification still fires.

In commit "validation: return block-file flush errors" (12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056)

> I wrote a test where a first flush fails and requests shutdown, then I fix the file and call `FlushStateToDisk()` again: it succeeds and `m_last_flushed_block` moves forward, even though shutdown was already requested before this second call. Is this expected?

Yes, this seems expected and good. The node still shuts down, but if the problem has cleared by then, the shutdown flush can save what the failed flush skipped.

When the block file flush fails, `FlushStateToDisk()` now returns without writing the block index or the coins, but that data stays in memory. `flushError()` requests shutdown, and `Shutdown()` in `init.cpp` then calls `ForceFlushStateToDisk()` on each chainstate. If the problem has cleared by then (say, file descriptors released as connections close), that flush writes everything. That's what the PR description means by "Later flushes can retry and write if they succeed, including during shutdown."

The flush doesn't check the interrupt before writing; it's checked by code that produces new state, like `ActivateBestChain()`. And `m_last_flushed_block` advancing on that flush is right: that flush succeeded, and with this PR the marker only moves on a successful flush.

I'd leave out the `Assume(m_chainman.m_interrupt)`, because it would fire for kernel API users on an ordinary flush failure.

The comment promises that the notification was sent, not that shutdown was requested. In the node, `flushError()` does request shutdown, but in the kernel API it's just a user callback, and nothing sets the interrupt unless the application does. A better way to check the invariant is a test that a failed `FlushBlockFile()` always calls `flushError()`, which #35731 adds.

In commit "validation: return block-file flush errors" (12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056)

Non-blocking, fine as a follow-up: if this early return happens during a prune flush and a later flush succeeds, the pruned block files are never deleted. They stay on disk until a reindex.

How it happens:

- `FindFilesToPrune()` has already marked the files pruned in memory (`PruneOneBlockFile()`) before the block-file flush runs, and `setFilesToPrune` is local to this call.
- The later flush writes the block index with those files marked pruned, but `FindFilesToPrune()` skips files with `nSize == 0`, so nothing finds them again.

Before this PR a block-file flush failure still unlinked them (the disk-space return above already had this gap).

It's only leaked disk space, not corruption. A fix could keep the pending set in a member that the next successful flush drains, or there could at least be a comment here noting the gap.

In commit "validation: return block-file flush errors" (12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056)

Note: one consequence of returning here that's easy to miss. When this happens inside [`ConnectTip()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056/src/validation.cpp#L3060-L3071) or [`DisconnectTip()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056/src/validation.cpp#L2959-L2978), the block has already been applied to `CoinsTip()` but `m_chain` isn't updated, so the coins tip and the chain tip disagree until shutdown.

Neither `ActivateBestChain()` nor mempool acceptance checks the interrupt first, so a transaction or block arriving before the network threads stop could hit the asserts in [`PreChecks()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056/src/validation.cpp#L876) or [`ConnectBlock()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056/src/validation.cpp#L2332), and the node would abort instead of shutting down cleanly. I found this by reading the code and haven't tried to reproduce it.

I don't think it should block this PR. It isn't corruption: the disk is still at the last successful flush, so the node recovers on restart the same way it would after a crash. And the `CheckDiskSpace()` return above could already get into this state.

For a follow-up, I think a better fix than adding interrupt checks to every path that assumes the coins tip matches the chain tip is to keep the in-memory state consistent. Memory and disk each need to be consistent on their own, but disk normally lags behind memory, and a failed flush only means it lags further. It shouldn't undo a change already made in memory. So I think `ConnectTip()` and `DisconnectTip()` should ignore the flush result the way [`AcceptBlock()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056/src/validation.cpp#L4399-L4405) does, since the error is already reported and the block really has been applied, and let `ActivateBestChain()` stop on the interrupt as usual. Returning before `SetTip()` dates from when every block was written to disk before memory was updated; that stopped being true when flushing became periodic in #5241, but the early return stayed.
